essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: The Artifact: Tyler's viral thread introducing the 'procedural generation' metaphor for psychospiritual introspection (Aug 2024, 1566 likes)
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
Possible huge problem with psychospiritual journeys: Yes, there are deep structures in the labyrinth of my mind, and yes, I will have profound insights and fundamental shifts when I bring them into full awareness...

And yet...after years of self-work, I'm starting to suspect a large amount of the labyrinth is actually *procedurally generated.* Like a video game map that builds itself on the spot the further you travel across it

It would be like this sequence playing out:
1. I dive deep into the labyrinth of my mind
2. The mind goes "Oh! He's expecting to find some deep structures. Let me generate some of those that are consistent with the rest of me. Oh! He's also expecting to find some enemies there, so let me spawn some demons."
3. Lo and behold, there is more (eg) "unresolved trauma" to resolve

I think that this process is especially responsive to my motivation. So if I *want* to be in the narrative of Psychospiritual Journey, complete with Shocking Moments Of Insight? (subtext: ...so that I can procrastinate Finding A Job, Building Relationships, Pursuing My Big Scary Calling, etc) ...Well, then the mind will be happy to help. It will procedurally generate an infinite psychospiritual landscape for me to "discover"

I suspect the dynamic I describe above is why many psychospiritual delvers seem like they're just moving in circles. Yes, the mind is vast and there's tons of actually wild stuff in there to explore. Yes, imho Mind is humanity's true final frontier. But also...in some important way...you might be making it up

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: First synthesis: Tyler proposes 'generator functions' as the efficient alternative to exploring recursive structures
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
a. It can be done way more efficiently!!
Instead of spending so much time exploring recursive "deep structures," instead you look for generator functions

You can see generator functions most clearly in people who are having a bad trip on psychedelics or via psychosis: they keep generating new reasons to be paranoid. If it turns out the government isn't watching them, then it's actually that evil spirits toying with them, etc.

Just keep in mind that – if you try to analyze the structure of a generator function – it will often go brrrrr on itself, and generate infinite recursive structure for you explore. Often better to hold off on analysis when you find it, and instead just lovingly "sit" with it / find the presence of awareness within it instead of trying to understand it

(Analysis also sometimes has the negative side effect of calcifying this structures through reification. It's like you turn a changeable ~liquid thing – the generator function – into a stable solid thing. And then you're stuck with a solid thing yikes. Luckily loving presence can convert it back to liquid)

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Practical application: Tyler experiments with renouncing IFS 'Parts' model in favor of unitary Will (Jan 2025)
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
As an experiment, I am renouncing the view that I am an amalgam of differently motivated Parts. Instead, I am a unitary Will

As a unitary Will there is no such thing as “being blocked” (eg unable to write or do admin or relax) due to conflicting motivations

Instead there are three options:

Yes:
I will do X (bc I want to)

No:
I won’t do X (bc I don’t want to)

Simmer/percolate/marinate:
I will postpone the decision of whether to do X right now. Maybe I need more information or I’m not in a good state to decide. So I postpone, understanding that I am CHOOSING inaction

Important for this approach: there is *no inner conflict* because there is only one Will (albeit you might be confused about how to channel it bc you are complex). It helps to get in touch with the *experience* of that unitary Will. It will typically be much bigger/wider than your ordinary sense of yourself

Had tried this for a day so far, modeling myself as a unitary Will feels much cleaner than the IFS-style introspection I was doing before. I’m pretty sure that by imagining that I consisted of conflicting Parts that I was hallucinating all sorts of inner conflict the way an LLM would if you prompted it to mediate between parts. (In a mediation frame, conflict is *assumed*)

Try it & report back
 or [emblematic of what I truly actually want to be doing]]

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Application to 'Imaginal Christianity': Tyler uses framework to analyze emerging mystical Christian movement (Jun 2025)
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
There’s an emerging branch of mystical Christianity that is very intriguing. I think of it as “Imaginal Christianity” (IC). You could also call it Mythic Christianity or Jungian Christianity

IC’s main selling point is that it’s compatible with a scientific mindset. I list the tenets I’ve observed below. By doing so, I try to document what I see ppl practicing. (I am not an Imaginal Christian.)

God = the ground of being. It is both presence and void, shows its love by embracing all things that exist & affording the path to salvation through communion with it

“The Lord”: a useful anthropomorphism of god. ICs use imagination to turn something incomprehensible (god) into an imaginal presence that we can speak to and which speaks to us through words, silence, and beyond

Jesus of Nazareth: a person who came much closer than most people to theosis – ie embodying how god would behave if it acted in human form with full recognition of its own nature. By doing so, Jesus genuinely did show us a path to salvation. (Although – here’s the heretical part – other people like Gautama Buddha might show us a complementary paths.) Thanks to the degree that Jesus was charismatic and the degree to which his followers admired him, they created and/or realized an imaginal being called Christ

Christ: a mind that continues to guide humans to salvation, directly inspired by Jesus of Nazareth (whose body is now dead). There are many names for the nature of this type of mind: thoughtform, tulpa, egregore, archetype, living symbol, yidam, memetic entity. His metaphysical status is similar to the way Tibetan lamas seem to regard their deities, as manifestations of Mind. This doesn’t make him less divine; he represents a latent divine potential available to all people. We see archetypes similar to Christ manifest across cultures: Osiris, Dionysus, Krishna, etc. However, Christ is is our culture’s instantiation of the archetype – his specific teachings and the story of his life are meaningful to us

The Bible: to be interpreted symbolically and read as a source of deep wisdom. Its story and teachings contain metaphors that powerfully interact with our collective consciousness. It is not read as an account of 100% literal happenings. It is also understood that the bible is contextual, created for a particular time and place, so it’s up to us to do careful translation and understand how to adapt it to our own context

Miracles & the supernatural: there is agnosticism about the metaphysical status of such things (eg virgin birth, the resurrection, heaven). They are at least seen as helpful metaphors. Some people who practice IC just shrug their shoulders and embrace mystery around the supernatural. Others attempt to retcon it through explanations that are compatible with scientific materialism (eg the idea that Jesus was a master bodyworker able to induce psychosomatic healing; or that hell is real but only as a state of mind)

Christ consciousness/Imitatio Christi: similar to Tibetan yidam practice, you can use imagination to take on the aspect/energy/mind of Christ. (Romans 13:14 – “Put on the Lord Jesus Christ”.) You can also do this with other imaginal beings like Mother Mary, Saint Francis, etc

Prayer: depending on who you ask, prayer is either:
(a) prompt engineering for your unconscious (you adopt benevolent intentions and they unconsciously affect behavior in positive and sometimes contagious ways)
(b) heart-led concentration meditation similar to metta
(c) interfacing with positive imaginal entities like Christ or angels or your personal anthropomorphism of god
(d) other things, or all of the above

Overall, I think IC is a positive development. Trad Christians will probably see it as quite heretical. And in my next post, I list some ways it could go wrong. But it could provide shared meaning to millions of Westerners who would otherwise be depressive atheists. IC harnesses the mythic language that people in the West already grew up with

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Synthesis: Tyler warns ICs about 'procedural generation of mental content' while acknowledging utility of imaginal practices
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
WAYS I SEE IMAGINAL CHRISTIANITY GOING WRONG:

Going Schizo with Entities
Christianity offers a whole cinematic universe of entities: angels, demons, Satan, etc. Similar to Christ, these are seen by ICs as imaginal beings who have their own partial autonomy in our collective consciousness. This is where I see IC practitioners going REAL crazy. They attribute way too much power to these entities, not understanding the degree to which they are belief-mediated. So the more power you believe a mental “demon” has, the more power you give it. I watch people engaging in all sorts of elaborate “magical” practices here to navigate the world of entities. I recommend instead just dissolving their supposed influence through practices of love, prayer, logic, clowning, or Buddhist-style emptiness. These practices are way less ego-pleasing than a narrative that you are engaged in magical trials with powerful entities. But they are less likely to drive you crazy

Procedural Generation of Mental Content
Similar to my last point, it’s important to recognize that the mind is really good at making stuff up. You might start practicing IC, and then start believing that “the angels told me to buy crypto” or “Satan made me behave badly toward my mom.” I think a better recipe for sanity is to hold the paradoxical belief there are mental entities who can guide you AND it’s also often just your imagination inventing nonsense. (See quoted post)

Christian Sinning 2.0
IC mostly just changes the metaphysical status of elements of Christianity, making them palatable to the modern mind. IC might still attract and create practitioners who fall victim to the worst Christian sins: self-righteousness & moralizing; judgement of outgroups; self-coercion, repression, and shame; establishment of oppressive hierarchies, and so on. It will take a broader effort to dissolve these negative patterns that seem to have plagued Christianity since it became entangled with state power
